samples.summary: Group drop guard silently discards animations that target the dropped group
samples.evidence: `if (!children) return ''` removes the `<p:grpSp>` from the spTree, so no `<p:cNvPr id="0" name="<groupId>">` is emitted for it. `renumberCNvPrIds` (slide.ts:110) therefore never adds the group id to `spidMap`, and `animationsToTimingXml` (animation.ts:321-322) does `if (spid === undefined) continue` — any SlideAnimation whose `elementId` is the emptied group is silently dropped from the exported timing, with no report through `opts.onImageError` or any other channel. Behaviour is consistent with per-element drops, but it is a new, unreported loss introduced by this guard (previously the group was emitted and the animation survived).

samples.summary: Comment's OOXML claim (empty <p:grpSp> is invalid) is likely incorrect
samples.evidence: The comment states "A `<p:grpSp>` with no shape children is not valid OOXML — PowerPoint rejects the part rather than ignoring the empty group." In ECMA-376 CT_GroupShape the shape-choice group is minOccurs=0/maxOccurs=unbounded, so `nvGrpSpPr` + `grpSpPr` alone is schema-valid. The behaviour (dropping the empty group) is harmless either way, but the stated justification is probably wrong and will mislead the next reader/reviewer about what is required.

samples.summary: groupToXml still crashes on a persisted group whose `children` is missing/non-array
samples.evidence: `data.children.map(...)` runs before the new emptiness guard and throws `TypeError: data.children.map is not a function` if the persisted GroupElement has no `children` array. The rest of this export module deliberately hardens against arbitrary persisted JSON (Map lookups with fallbacks in animation.ts:60-69, `toXmlInt` at animation.ts:82) precisely because the content PUT API can persist anything; the new guard added directly below this line does not cover the degenerate `children: undefined`/`children: {}` case, which aborts the whole deck export rather than dropping one element the way the guard intends. Pre-existing line, but adjacent to and in the same failure class as the change.
